On this page

Neat uses the GenAI APIs for LLM, VLM, and ASR models prepared with LLiMa. This
is the generative-model counterpart to
[`Model`](https://developer.sima.ai/software/develop-apps/development-workflow/model): load a deployed model
directory, create a request, then run it inside your application or serve it
over HTTP. For applications on a host machine connected to a Modalix PCIe Card,
use the [PCIe GenAI APIs](https://developer.sima.ai/software/develop-apps/development-workflow/genai-model/pcie-api).

Use these APIs when your application asks a model to generate text, answer
questions about images, call tools, or transcribe audio. Use the classic
`Model` API for fixed-shape discriminative models such as classification,
detection, segmentation, or embedding models.

## Where GenAI fits [​](https://developer.sima.ai/software/develop-apps/development-workflow/genai-model\#where-genai-fits "Direct link to Where GenAI fits")

The GenAI path has the same high-level shape as the rest of Neat:

1. Prepare or download a model artifact for Modalix.
2. Put the model on the target, commonly under `/media/nvme/llima/models/`, or
keep it on your host machine for PCIe execution.
3. Load the model from your C++ or Python application.
4. Send a request directly or expose the model through `GenAIServer`.
5. Read the complete result or consume streamed output.

LLiMa owns GenAI model preparation, command-line testing, and benchmarking.
Neat owns the application-facing API and runtime integration once the model is
used inside your app. For model preparation details, see
[GenAI with LLiMa](https://developer.sima.ai/software/genai-llima/).

## Choose an application boundary [​](https://developer.sima.ai/software/develop-apps/development-workflow/genai-model\#choose-an-application-boundary "Direct link to Choose an application boundary")

## Serve applications and clients

Recommended for most applications. Use the GenAI server to expose common API endpoints.

- [**GenAI Server** Register one or more models and call OpenAI- or Ollama-compatible HTTP endpoints.](https://developer.sima.ai/software/develop-apps/development-workflow/genai-model/genai-server/)

## Run in your process

Use the direct APIs when your C++ or Python application owns the model call.

- [**Direct GenAI APIs** Run or stream LLM, VLM, and ASR requests in process, and compose GenAI graph fragments.](https://developer.sima.ai/software/develop-apps/development-workflow/genai-model/direct-api/)

Use direct calls for embedded application logic and tests that should run in
the same process as the model. Use the server when clients should not link
against the Neat runtime or when one process should route requests to multiple
served models.

## Next steps [​](https://developer.sima.ai/software/develop-apps/development-workflow/genai-model\#next-steps "Direct link to Next steps")

- Run models from a host machine with the [PCIe GenAI APIs](https://developer.sima.ai/software/develop-apps/development-workflow/genai-model/pcie-api).
- Follow [Serve GenAI Models](https://developer.sima.ai/software/tutorials/serve-genai-models) for a complete HTTP server example.
- Follow [Run an LLM with the Direct API](https://developer.sima.ai/software/tutorials/run-an-llm) for an in-process walkthrough.
- Prepare and benchmark models with [GenAI with LLiMa](https://developer.sima.ai/software/genai-llima/).
